brand_platform.positioning: For Myanmar and Singapore business owners who are tired of paying for posts instead of results, ZYNTH is the agency that runs on an AI workforce with one human accountable — unlike traditional agencies, we show the thinking, the numbers and the margin behind every campaign.
brand_platform.promise: Every piece of work we ship can be traced to a number the client already cares about — and we will show that number whether it flatters us or not.

audience.insight: Marketing spend is the only line on a Myanmar SME's P&L that nobody can defend in a meeting. Owners don't distrust agencies because the work is ugly — they distrust it because they cannot see inside it. The brand that shows its own working, including its margin and its failures, stops being a vendor and becomes the person they call before they decide anything.

Our agency's status meeting was replaced by a 5:30am brief written by an AI workforce. One human still signs everything.

Twelve agents. Research, creative, media, finance, operations. They run overnight, argue with each other through a shared memory, and put a brief on the desk before the city is awake. Nothing reaches a client until the MD approves it — that has never changed and won't.

What it buys our clients isn't cheaper work. It's a bigger team than our headcount, working on their brand at 3am, and a founder who has the time to think instead of chase.

We'll keep showing how it works. That's the point.

posts.hook: Three numbers we check before we take your money. If they don't work, we say no.
posts.caption_en:
Three numbers we check before we take your money. If they don't work, we say no.

1. What one customer is worth to you over a year. Not one sale — a year.
2. What you can afford to pay to get one. If that number is smaller than the platform's cost per lead in your category, no campaign fixes it.
3. Your margin. A 12% margin business cannot buy growth with paid media. It has to earn it with content and referral first.

We've turned down work on number 3 more than once. It's cheaper for everyone than six months of blaming the creative.

posts.hook: "Facebook is where everyone is" is not a strategy. It's a starting condition.
posts.caption_en:
"Facebook is where everyone is" is not a strategy. It's a starting condition.

Everyone's competitor is on the same platform, buying the same placements, targeting the same city. Being present is table stakes. The decision that actually moves your number is what you do with the 3 seconds you rent.

Three things that change results more than the platform choice:
· A first line written for one person, not an audience
· Myanmar text that reads like a person wrote it, not a translation tool
· A single CTA — the moment there are two, both get ignored

Platform is the room. The message is whether anyone turns around.

How we price a campaign — including our margin. Yes, the actual number.

Every quote we issue is built the same way: production at real supplier cost, a 10% contingency line that is never quietly spent, a management fee, and a 35% margin floor below which we don't take the job. Not because we're greedy — because an agency working under 35% starts cutting the parts of the work the client can't see.

Everything converts at market FX, sell side. Never the official rate. If a quote uses the official rate, someone is absorbing a loss and it will show up in your delivery.

Swipe for the structure. Copy it — we'd rather the whole market quoted properly.

posts.hook: If your marketing budget is written at the official exchange rate, your budget is fiction.
posts.caption_en:
If your marketing budget is written at the official exchange rate, your budget is fiction.

Every supplier you'll actually pay — printers, production crews, LED vendors, imported materials — prices against the market rate. Budget at the official rate and the gap shows up halfway through the campaign, usually as a quality cut nobody admits to.

Two habits that fix it:
· Write every budget line at the market rate, sell side, and date the rate you used
· Carry a 10% contingency that is a line item, not a hope

It doesn't make the campaign cheaper. It makes the number true.

posts.hook: The hardest part of running an AI workforce isn't the AI. It's deciding what a human must still own.
posts.caption_en:
The hardest part of running an AI workforce isn't the AI. It's deciding what a human must still own.

Ours owns four things, permanently:
· Any number that reaches a client — if we can't verify it, it ships tagged unverified or it doesn't ship
· Anything that leaves the building — every email, every proposal, approved by a person
· Saying no to work we shouldn't take
· The relationship. Nobody wants a quarterly review with a workflow.

Everything else — research, drafting, structuring, costing, calendars — the agents do faster and more consistently than we did manually. Pretending otherwise would be its own kind of dishonesty.

design_system.art_direction: Editorial, not promotional. Every asset should look like a page torn from a well-set business document rather than a social graphic — deep navy fields, generous margins, one gold accent doing one job per frame. The work is confident enough to be quiet: no gradients, no glow, no stock imagery of people pointing at laptops. Where photography appears it is real work, real rooms, real Yangon light. The system's job is to make a small agency look like the most rigorous one in the room, at thumbnail size, on a mid-range Android in daylight.

typography.headline: A confident geometric sans (Inter Tight / Söhne class), 600–700 weight. Feed headline 44–72pt at 1080px canvas. Sentence case, never all-caps except the IGNITE wordmark. Maximum 9 words — if it needs 10, the copy is wrong, not the layout.
typography.body: Same family, 400 weight, 24–30pt at 1080px, line-height 1.45, measure capped at 34 characters on square formats. Left-aligned always; centred body text is banned in this system.
typography.myanmar: Pyidaungsu (or Noto Sans Myanmar) — never a Latin face with Myanmar glyphs faked in. Line-height 1.9 minimum to clear stacked diacritics, and 15% larger optical size than the Latin equivalent to match perceived weight. Myanmar and English never share a line; they stack, with a 24px gold rule between them. Never letter-space Myanmar text.
typography.hierarchy_rules: One idea per frame, three levels maximum: headline, one supporting line, one CTA chip. Numbers are typographic events — when a frame has a number worth reading (12, 16, 35%, 50 days), it is set 2–3× the headline size and everything else recedes.

layout_rules: One gold element per frame. If a second wants to exist, the first one wasn't doing its job.
Headline maximum 9 words, and it must be legible when the asset is 120px wide — check every frame at that size before it ships.
Bottom 220px of any 4:5 asset stays clear of critical content (feed UI, caption fold).
Myanmar text never shares a line with English; it stacks below, separated by a 24px gold rule, at 1.9 line-height.
No icons in Ledger or Statement templates. Icons are permitted only in Teach, at 32px, single-weight, and never more than three per frame.
No drop shadows, no gradients, no glass effects, no glow. Depth comes from the field change, not from an effect.
Photography is real or it is absent. Generated imagery may only ever be an abstract background or texture — never a person, product, premises or result presented as real.
design_system.photography_direction: Documentary, available light, slightly underexposed to keep navy shadows rich. Real desks, real Yangon rooms, real crew at work — the camera is an observer, never a director. Hands and screens over faces where a face isn't necessary. Colour graded cool in the shadows so it sits with the navy field; skin tones stay natural, never teal. No smiling stock, no handshakes, no laptops on cafe tables with nothing on the screen.
graphic_devices: The gold entry rule — 4px × 120px, sits above every headline, the system's signature mark
The number as hero — figures set 2–3× headline size, the only permitted 'loud' element
The strike-through in gold — used exclusively to show what was cut or corrected (P05, P07)
The interval bracket — two rules with a gap, used to show a gap between two values (P13 FX)
The colour flip — carousel takeaway frames invert from off-white to navy, marking the ending
design_system.accessibility: Off-white #F5F3EF on navy #12203A = 13.1:1, and charcoal #2B2B2B on off-white = 13.6:1 — both far clear of WCAG AA. Gold #B88A2A on navy is 4.9:1: acceptable for headlines and large numbers, never for body text or anything below 24pt. Minimum on-asset text size 24pt at 1080px canvas. Every video carries burned-in subtitles in both languages (sound-off is the default), minimum 32pt with a 60%-opacity navy scrim behind. Every published asset also needs alt text — written by whoever schedules it, in the caption's primary language.
